rule.description: A method whose body primarily accesses one foreign named struct owner's fields (at least 3 accesses across at least 3 distinct fields, more than twice its own owner accesses) is envious: the behavior belongs with the data it uses.

checks.description: Detect methods whose bodies concentrate field access on one foreign named struct owner, dominating the method's access to its own receiver's owner type.
checks.detected_relation: method receiver owner -> primarily accessed foreign struct owner
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The method's home owner defines behavior whose data almost entirely belongs to a different owner, so the behavior is misplaced across the ownership boundary and belongs with the data it accesses.

matches.evidence: Session.streamConsumed mutates and reads the stream receive counters (numRead, incr) and consults windowUpdateThreshold while making no field access to its own owner.
Session.streamWindow derives the v2 send window from the stream's written, consumed and advertised window counters, all owned by stream, with no access to its own owner's fields.

After a registry lookup of only 3 own-owner accesses, the snapshot construction reads stream identity, read/written counters, window state and lifecycle channels (8 distinct stream fields, 9 accesses).
Session.ShaperBacklog reads the shaper queue's pending count, round-robin list and per-stream heap table to aggregate queued bytes, reaching through its own owner only once for the queue handle.
stream.bufferedBytes takes a descriptor alias of its own ring handle and then scans the ring's size, head, mask and slots, dominating its single own-owner access.

excluded.reason: Frame serialization accesses concentrate on request/result values held in local control flow while the method's own socket, shaper and error state dominates the body; no single foreign owner reaches the dominance relation.
These call sites reach other components through operations and their own stream fields, not through repeated raw field selection on a foreign owner.

Field stores into the locally constructed accounting result value are output construction by the method itself, not access to a foreign object's state, and are excluded from the dominance comparison by the rule.
Config is a shared parameter object consulted broadly; accesses never concentrate on one owner's data strongly enough to form the relation.
